root_causes.description: Follow state fetched per item inside the profile serializer instead of once per response
No server-side bound on list result sizes (unclamped limit; unpaginated comments and tags)
Write through a second connection while the request's own SQLite read transaction is open (lock inversion)
Schema declares no indexes on hot filter/join columns; AutoMigrate creates only declared indexes
SQLite single-writer engine run with default locking configuration, uncapped pool, and read-only transactions
Auth middleware registered twice on the same route group

findings.problem: Each article in a list response (and each comment in a comment list) is serialized through ProfileSerializer.Response, which issues one isFollowing SELECT on follow_models per item. Favorite state on the same path is batched; follow state is not.
findings.performance_principle: Per-response work should not scale with item count when the per-item fact can be fetched for the whole set in one round trip.

evidence.statement: Loop over s.Articles calls ResponseWithPreloaded per article
ProfileSerializer.Response sets Following: myUserModel.isFollowing(...), one DB query per call
CommentsSerializer.Response loops all comments, each calling authorSerializer.Response()
Derived: extra queries per list response = n (page size, default 20 from articles/models.go:189, client-controlled); per comment list = number of comments (unbounded)
No runtime evidence (no query log, trace, or profile supplied)

findings.conditions: List endpoints (/api/articles, /api/articles/feed, /api/articles/:slug/comments) carry meaningful traffic and pages or comment threads exceed a handful of items. Traffic is unknown; at the default page size this is 20 extra queries per list request.

counter_evidence.statement: Searched for batching of follow state next to BatchGetFavoriteStatus: none
Searched for per-request memoization of isFollowing: none
SQLite is embedded (no network RTT), bounding absolute per-query cost but not growth

findings.why_this_might_not_matter: With in-process SQLite and indexed point lookups, 20 extra queries may be a small share of request time; no profile shows it dominates.
findings.recommendation: Add a batch follow-status lookup (one SELECT following_id FROM follow_models WHERE followed_by_id = ? AND following_id IN ?) per response, inject the result into the profile serializer, and skip it entirely for anonymous viewers (ID 0). Apply the same to CommentsSerializer.

alternatives.option: Batch follow status per response; skip for anonymous viewers
alternatives.why: Removes the work; one query regardless of n; mirrors the existing BatchGetFavoriteStatus pattern

alternatives.option: Per-request memo keyed by author ID

findings.trade_offs: Changes the serializer API (following state injected). IN-list size is bounded by page size, which relies on PERF-002 being fixed.

findings.problem: In the author and favorited branches, FindManyArticle opens a transaction, reads through it, then calls GetArticleUserModel which runs FirstOrCreate through the global handle on a different pooled connection. If the row is missing, that INSERT cannot commit in rollback-journal mode while the same goroutine's open transaction holds a SHARED lock: the request waits on itself while holding RESERVED/PENDING locks on the whole database file.
findings.performance_principle: Do not wait, inside a critical section, for a resource the critical section itself prevents from becoming available.

evidence.statement: GetArticleUserModel called while tx open (author branch)
GetArticleUserModel uses common.GetDB() (not tx) and FirstOrCreate; error ignored
No journal_mode, busy_timeout, or SetMaxOpenConns configured
Mechanism derived from SQLite's documented rollback-journal locking; not reproduced. No runtime evidence.

findings.conditions: SQLite in rollback-journal mode (no WAL configured), a non-zero effective busy timeout, and list requests filtering by an existing user who has no article_user_models row. A failed INSERT leaves no row, so the condition repeats. Workload and deployment unknown; confidence capped at Medium.

counter_evidence.statement: Searched for WAL pragma or DSN params: none
Tests always create the ArticleUserModel before author/favorited filtering; '?author=someauthor' names a nonexistent user so GetArticleUserModel returns early. No test exercises the trigger
AGENTS.md describes SQLite as for development/testing; if never used in production the blast radius disappears
Effective busy timeout unknown; with zero it becomes an immediate wrong empty result rather than a stall

findings.why_this_might_not_matter: If SQLite is dev-only, or the effective busy timeout is zero, there is no stall; users without an article_user_models row are uncommon in an active deployment.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the user and its ArticleUserModel before db.Begin() as a pure lookup (no create), and drop the explicit transaction from this read-only path.

alternatives.option: Lookup-only ArticleUserModel before/without the tx; drop read tx
alternatives.why: Removes both the write-on-read and the lock inversion with the fewest moving parts

findings.trade_offs: Without the read tx, articlesCount and the page may disagree by a row under concurrent writes; users without a row are no longer auto-created by others' list requests.

validation.expectation: Before: roughly the driver busy timeout or a BUSY error. After: immediate.
validation.falsifier: Before the fix the call returns immediately and an article_user_models row exists afterwards.
validation.guard: Keep that test with a completion-time bound and correct empty result

findings.problem: Columns filtered on every request have no declared index: follow_models(following_id, followed_by_id), favorite_models(favorite_id, favorite_by_id), article_models.author_id, comment_models.article_id, article_user_models.user_model_id, users.username. Each lookup is a full scan of a table that only grows (soft deletes), and PERF-001 multiplies the follow scan per item.
findings.performance_principle: Per-request lookups should cost in proportion to the result, not to the table.

findings.why_this_might_not_matter: A demo-sized database may hold tens to hundreds of rows, where scans are effectively free and every index is pure write overhead on a single-writer engine.
findings.recommendation: Run EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN per hot query on a representative copy; add composite indexes in model tags only where plans show SCAN (likely follow_models(followed_by_id, following_id), favorite_models(favorite_id, favorite_by_id), article_models(author_id, updated_at), comment_models(article_id), unique article_user_models(user_model_id), unique users(username), article_tags(tag_model_id)); run ANALYZE afterwards.

alternatives.option: Plan-driven composite indexes declared in model tags
alternatives.why: Turns scans into probes and is versioned with the code

findings.trade_offs: Each index adds write cost on a single-writer engine and file size; a unique username index fails if duplicates exist; building an index on a large live file holds the write lock.

findings.problem: SQLite is opened with no journal_mode, no busy_timeout and no SetMaxOpenConns; read-only list/feed paths run inside explicit transactions, lengthening shared-lock holds that block writer commits in rollback-journal mode.
findings.performance_principle: On a single-writer resource, minimize lock hold time and the number of concurrent contenders.

evidence.statement: No PRAGMA anywhere in repo. No runtime evidence.

findings.conditions: Production on SQLite with concurrent writes overlapping list reads. Deployment and write concurrency unknown; confidence capped at Medium.

counter_evidence.statement: Driver may apply its own default busy timeout; not verified
Searched for WAL or DSN settings: none

findings.why_this_might_not_matter: Low write concurrency or a dev-only deployment never produces contention; a move to a client-server RDBMS makes this moot.
findings.recommendation: If SQLite stays: enable WAL, set an explicit measured busy_timeout, cap open connections deliberately, and remove explicit transactions from read-only paths. If concurrent writers at scale are needed, revisit the engine choice with workload data.

alternatives.option: WAL + explicit busy_timeout + drop read transactions
alternatives.why: Removes reader/writer blocking at low cost

findings.trade_offs: WAL adds -wal/-shm files and checkpoint management and is unsafe on network filesystems; busy_timeout trades errors for latency.

validation.metric: PRAGMA journal_mode / busy_timeout values and count of 'database is locked' log lines under concurrent writes
validation.expectation: Fewer lock errors and lower list-endpoint tail latency under concurrent writes after the change.
validation.falsifier: A staging concurrency test shows no lock errors or waits before the change.
validation.guard: Alert on 'database is locked' in logs
